note: A round freezes these ceilings and its measured starting size when it opens. For ordinary rounds, `prune` rejects growth beyond the higher of those two values; inherited overage remains visible in `health` and cannot be worsened. An explicit budget-change round may revise ceilings and is RECORDED after clean checks, never credited with a repair. Historical raises and ratchets remain records; close no longer ratchets automatically.

raises.reason: The loop's own guarantees had to be written where a reader of this skill will meet them — references/behavior-evaluation.md — including the three lines that say which guards are convention rather than enforcement. Spending 43 lines of the budget on stating a limit honestly is the trade this ceiling exists to make visible, not to prevent.

The derivation gained write-back (`--emit`), the reverse projection behind `contract-migrate`, and one drift code per derived field. Those 98 lines are the generator's write side; the read side they serve removed far more from the documents than they add here, which is the trade this ceiling exists to surface rather than to block.

A universal claim with no declared universe was accepted everywhere outside a migration. Fifteen lines close that, and the gate stopping the release over seven of them is the ceiling doing its job: the trade is now written down instead of drifting.

Two changes that pay for themselves in the documents rather than here. `resolveDerivable` lets a document that wrote a requirement table omit the JSON copy entirely — the logger SDD lost 94 contract lines to it, more than this raise costs. `readDeclarations` reads an exported surface from a document's own fences when it has no canonical API section, taking the type probe from 8 documents of 83 to 36.

sdd/v2 adds its contract, program and migration pages while every v1 page stays for existing sdd-loop-delivery/v1 documents (migai still has live .loop.json deliveries). The rest of the raise pays for the v2 authoring map that absorbs spec-kit (constitution, clarify, prioritized stories, checklist, analyze) into the six phases, the restored conditional guide table and a diagnostic routing table for both routes.

The v2 validator (v2-document.ts, v2-meta.ts) is a second route beside the legacy v1 validator until v1 retires. Its 110 original codes were consolidated to 18 families before this round; the remainder of the raise pays for derived single-document Meta, optional repository location, table-definition precedence, clarification tracking, read-path existence and priority/wave projection.

The previous ceiling was reached by compaction, leaving no room; the raise is sized to the two checks plus their comments.
